from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Introduction: What is a Vector?", [
            "Vectors have both magnitude and direction.",
            "Scalars possess only magnitude, like numbers.",
            "Vectors are represented in a coordinate plane."
        ])
        
        # Coordinates
        origin = self.grid["F1"]
        end_point = self.grid["C4"]
        
        # Create Vector
        vector = Arrow(start=origin, end=end_point, color=WHITE, buff=0)
        label_v = Text("v", color=WHITE, font_size=24).next_to(vector.get_center(), UP)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(vector), Write(label_v))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFD700") # Gold color
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight arrow in red
        self.play(vector.animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF0000")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Draw components
        h_line = DashedLine(start=origin, end=np.array([end_point[0], origin[1], 0]), color="#00FF00")
        v_line = DashedLine(start=np.array([end_point[0], origin[1], 0]), end=end_point, color="#00FF00")
        label_x = Text("x", color="#00FF00", font_size=20).next_to(h_line.get_center(), DOWN)
        label_y = Text("y", color="#00FF00", font_size=20).next_to(v_line.get_center(), RIGHT)
        
        self.play(Create(h_line), Create(v_line), Write(label_x), Write(label_y))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Move vector
        new_end = self.grid["B5"]
        self.play(
            vector.animate.put_start_and_end_on(origin, new_end),
            label_v.animate.next_to(new_end, UP),
            h_line.animate.put_start_and_end_on(origin, np.array([new_end[0], origin[1], 0])),
            v_line.animate.put_start_and_end_on(np.array([new_end[0], origin[1], 0]), new_end),
            label_x.animate.next_to(np.array([new_end[0]/2 + origin[0]/2, origin[1], 0]), DOWN),
            label_y.animate.next_to(np.array([new_end[0], (new_end[1]+origin[1])/2, 0]), RIGHT)
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Flash components
        self.play(
            Flash(h_line.get_center(), color="#FFFF00"),
            Flash(v_line.get_center(), color="#FFFF00")
        )
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Vector Addition: The Tip-to-Tail Rule", [
            "Add vectors by connecting them tip-to-tail.", 
            "The resultant vector connects start to end.", 
            "Addition forms the diagonal of a parallelogram."
        ])
        
        # Setup vectors
        v_start = ORIGIN
        v_end = np.array([1.5, 0.5, 0])
        w_end = np.array([0.5, 1.5, 0])
        
        v = Arrow(v_start, v_end, color=WHITE, buff=0)
        w = Arrow(v_start, w_end, color=WHITE, buff=0)
        
        v_label = MathTex("v", color=WHITE).next_to(v.get_center(), UP, buff=0.1)
        w_label = MathTex("w", color=WHITE).next_to(w.get_center(), RIGHT, buff=0.1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(v), Create(w), Write(v_label), Write(w_label))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Slide w so its tail touches the tip of v
        w_shifted = Arrow(v_end, v_end + w_end, color=WHITE, buff=0)
        w_label_shifted = MathTex("w", color=WHITE).next_to(w_shifted.get_center(), RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(w, w_shifted), ReplacementTransform(w_label, w_label_shifted))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Draw resultant vector
        resultant = Arrow(v_start, v_end + w_end, color="#00FFFF", buff=0)
        res_label = MathTex("v+w", color="#00FFFF").next_to(resultant.get_center(), UP, buff=0.1)
        
        # Parallelogram visuals
        dashed_v = DashedLine(w_end, v_end + w_end, color=GRAY)
        dashed_w = DashedLine(v_end, v_end + w_end, color=GRAY)
        
        self.play(Create(resultant), Write(res_label))
        self.play(Create(dashed_v), Create(dashed_w))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Scalars change a vector's length.", "Negative scalars reverse a vector's direction.", "Multiplying stretches or compresses the vector."]
        self.setup_layout("Scalar Multiplication: Stretching and Flipping", lecture_lines)
        
        origin = self.grid["D3"]
        v = Arrow(origin, origin + RIGHT * 2, color=WHITE, buff=0)
        v_label = MathTex(r"\vec{v}", color=WHITE).next_to(v.get_end(), UP)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(v), Write(v_label))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        v2 = Arrow(origin, origin + RIGHT * 4, color="#00FF00", buff=0)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Linear Combinations: Spanning the Space", [
            "Any vector can reach any coordinate point.",
            "We use basis vectors i and j.",
            "Linear combinations span the 2D space."
        ])
        
        # Define base vectors i, j
        i_vec = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT, color=WHITE)
        j_vec = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=UP, color=WHITE)
        i_label = MathTex("\\vec{i}", color=WHITE).next_to(i_vec.get_end(), DOWN)
        j_label = MathTex("\\vec{j}", color=WHITE).next_to(j_vec.get_end(), LEFT)
        basis = VGroup(i_vec, j_vec, i_label, j_label)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.place_in_area(basis, 'B2', 'E5')
        self.play(Create(basis), self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        i_scaled = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=2*RIGHT, color="#00FF00")
        j_scaled = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=3*UP, color="#00FF00")
        i_scaled_label = MathTex("2\\vec{i}", color="#00FF00").next_to(i_scaled.get_end(), DOWN)
        j_scaled_label = MathTex("3\\vec{j}", color="#00FF00").next_to(j_scaled.get_end(), LEFT)
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(i_vec.copy(), i_scaled),
            ReplacementTransform(j_vec.copy(), j_scaled),
            FadeIn(i_scaled_label),
            FadeIn(j_scaled_label),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00")
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        sum_vec = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=2*RIGHT + 3*UP, color="#FFFF00")
        sum_label = MathTex("2\\vec{i} + 3\\vec{j}", color="#FFFF00").next_to(sum_vec.get_end(), RIGHT)
        
        self.play(
            Create(sum_vec),
            Write(sum_label),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00")
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Real-world Application", [
            "Vectors are foundational to linear algebra.",
            "They enable 3D graphics and rendering.",
            "Vectors drive modern AI neural networks."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        
        summary_group = VGroup(
            Text("Vectors", color=WHITE),
            Text("Addition", color=WHITE),
            Text("Scaling", color=WHITE),
            Text("Spans", color=WHITE)
        ).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT)
        self.place_in_area(summary_group, 'A1', 'C6', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(summary_group))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        
        # Simple representation of a 3D robot arm
        robot_arm = VGroup(
            Line(ORIGIN, UP*0.5, color=GREY),
            Dot(UP*0.5, color=BLUE),
            Line(UP*0.5, UP*0.5+RIGHT*0.5, color=GREY),
            Dot(UP*0.5+RIGHT*0.5, color=BLUE)
        )
        self.place_at_grid(robot_arm, 'D3', scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(Create(robot_arm))
        self.play(Rotate(robot_arm[2], angle=PI/4, about_point=robot_arm[0].get_end()))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        
        final_heading = Text("Vector Algebra", color="#FFFF00", font_size=40)
        self.place_at_grid(final_heading, 'F3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Flash(final_heading, color=YELLOW))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Fundamentals of Vectors and Linear Algebra

sections.title: Introduction: What is a Vector?
sections.content: Define vectors as entities possessing both magnitude and direction, contrasted with scalars (magnitude only). Introduce the coordinate plane representation (x, y).
sections.example: A GPS-guided drone flying 5km North (vector) versus a drone's battery level at 80% (scalar).

sections.title: Vector Addition: The Tip-to-Tail Rule
sections.content: Explain vector addition geometrically. Visualize the result as the diagonal of a parallelogram. Introduce the concept of resultant vectors.
sections.example: A cat walking 3 meters East, then 4 meters North. The 'resultant' path is the straight-line displacement from the start to the end point.

sections.title: Scalar Multiplication: Stretching and Flipping
sections.content: Discuss how multiplying a vector by a scalar changes its length or reverses its direction. Use a scaling factor (k) to show visual compression or expansion.
sections.example: A game character running at velocity V. If they get a 'Speed Boost' power-up, their velocity becomes 2V (doubling the vector length).

sections.title: Linear Combinations: Spanning the Space
sections.content: Explain that any vector in 2D can be reached by a combination of two basis vectors (i and j). Introduce the concept of linear span.
sections.example: A robotic arm with two joints; by adjusting the lengths (scalars) of its segments (basis vectors), the gripper can reach any point in its reachable workspace.

sections.title: Summary and Real-world Application
sections.content: Briefly recap vectors as the building blocks of Linear Algebra. Conclude by mentioning how these concepts form the foundation for 3D graphics and AI neural networks.
sections.example: Visualizing how pixels on a screen are essentially vectors being transformed and manipulated by matrix operations to render animations.
